clients.name: Northgate Coatings Ltd
clients.notes: Develops low-friction anti-corrosion coatings for offshore wind turbine bearings and subsea fixings. Wants to move from pilot line to qualified production. Has cash reserves and has said they would fund a match on a large collaborative project.

evidence.quote: We're developing a low-friction coating for offshore turbine bearings - the current products fail on salt-water ingress after about eighteen months.
If the project were the right one we could put in three or four hundred thousand of our own money over two years.
Strathclyde have been doing our salt-spray testing for two years now. Fairhaven Marine have looked at the samples but we've not got anything formal with them.
We were gutted about the Smart application but we'd go again with the right consortium.

clients.name: Vellum Bioelectronics Ltd
named_partners: Queen Elizabeth Hospital NHS Trust - clinical advisor
clients.notes: Building a biocompatible electrode coating for implantable neural interfaces. Spun out of a university but is a trading company. Clinical advisor at an NHS trust attends their advisory board.

evidence.quote: The core of it is a biocompatible interface layer that stops the scarring you normally get around a chronic implant.
We've got a consultant from the Queen Elizabeth on our advisory board - she sits in on the quarterly reviews.
Cash is the constraint. The Catalyst money runs to next summer and after that we need either revenue or another round.

clients.name: Harbrook Composites Ltd
clients.notes: Recyclable thermoplastic composite structures for aerospace interiors. Experienced consortium lead. Bid team is one person and is already committed to the ATI round this autumn.

evidence.quote: The whole pitch is a thermoplastic laminate you can actually reprocess at end of life, which nobody in interiors is doing at volume.
Honestly, between now and Christmas Dan is fully on the ATI bid. I couldn't put him on anything else.
Meridian take about sixty percent of our output and they've co-signed work packages with us before.

clients.name: Sable Photonics Ltd
clients.notes: Metasurface antenna elements for satcom terminals. Founder has been burned by the time cost of a previous grant application elsewhere and is sceptical of anything with a long form.

evidence.quote: Our metasurface layer replaces the phase shifter stack - it's the whole reason the terminal can be flat.
I spent six weeks on a grant application at my last company and got nothing for it. I'd need a very good reason to do that again.
There are two integrators evaluating our samples but I can't name them, we're under NDA.

clients.name: Tolmere Alloys Ltd
clients.notes: Nickel superalloy castings for high-temperature and extreme-environment applications, mainly energy and industrial gas turbines. Not spoken to since late 2025.

evidence.quote: Everything we cast is going into something that runs hot - turbine hot sections, mostly, and some downhole tooling.

clients.name: Ashcroft Institute for Materials Research
clients.notes: Independent research and technology organisation. Strong materials characterisation capability, often approached to join consortia. Cannot lead a business-led competition.

evidence.quote: We're an RTO - we can only ever be a partner on these, never the lead.

clients.name: Quenby Care Systems Ltd
clients.notes: Rostering and remote monitoring software for domiciliary care providers. No hardware, no materials work.

evidence.quote: It's pure software - we integrate with whatever monitoring kit the trust already has.

clients.name: Ledbury Payments Ltd
clients.notes: Cross-border payment reconciliation for SME exporters. Growth is a sales and funding question, not an R&D one.

evidence.quote: We're not really an R&D business any more - the platform works, it's about distribution now.
